name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Huge fundraising and cash-on-hand gap favoring Smith
Prediction markets price Smith near certain to win
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, Smith's long incumbency, and his dominant fundraising edge over an underfunded challenger all point to a safe Republican hold, and Polymarket prices Smith at roughly 96%. No polls or expert ratings contradict this picture.
model.watch: A late, well-funded outside spending surge for the challenger or a major scandal involving Smith could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chris Smith, one of the longest-serving House members, seeks another term in a New Jersey district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised nearly $600,000 and holding almost $490,000 on hand, while Democrat Rachel Peace has raised only about $34,000 with minimal cash remaining.

Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all align in pointing to a comfortable Republican victory, with the main open question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
